title: Finite-stage pair category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible, as required for the integral categories of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ be the directed poset of finite intermediate extensions $\Ql\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$ of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], ordered by inclusion. Here finite means finite-dimensional over $\Ql$, not finite as a set. It contains $\Ql$, and the compositum gives a common upper bound. For $E\subseteq F$ in $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$, put
$$
 \mathcal C_E(T)=\Dbc(T,E),
 \qquad T_{F/E}=F\otimes_E^L-:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_F(T),
$$
the categories $\Dbc(T,E)$ being those of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The normalized units
$T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$, the associators $a_{G,F,E}$, and the shift
comparisons $\sigma_{F/E}$ used below are the data constructed in
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Define an object of $\mathcal P_T$ to be a pair $(E,K)$ with
$K\in\mathcal C_E(T)$. A morphism representative
$(M,u):(E,K)\to(F,L)$ consists of a finite field $M\supseteq E,F$ and a map
$$
 u:T_{M/E}K\longrightarrow T_{M/F}L
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal C_M(T).
$$
Here $a_{N,M,E,K}$ denotes the component at $K$ of the natural isomorphism $a_{N,M,E}$. For $M\subseteq N$, transport it to
$$
 u_N=
 a_{N,M,F,L}\circ T_{N/M}(u)\circ a_{N,M,E,K}^{-1}.
$$
Representatives $(M,u)$ and $(N,v)$ are equivalent if $u_P=v_P$ in
$\mathcal C_P(T)$ for some finite $P\supseteq M,N$. Define
$$
 \Hom_{\mathcal P_T}((E,K),(F,L))
 =\varinjlim_{M\supseteq E,F}
 \Hom_{\mathcal C_M(T)}(T_{M/E}K,T_{M/F}L)
$$
as the resulting equivalence classes, or equivalently the directed colimit of abelian groups [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. The indexing poset consists of the finite overfields of $E$ and $F$; it is nonempty and directed since it contains $EF$ and is closed under taking composita.

Write a class as $[M,u]$. For two classes with the same source and target, choose a finite $P\supseteq M,N$ and prescribe
$$
 [M,u]+[N,v]=[P,u_P+v_P],\qquad
 -[M,u]=[M,-u],\qquad 0=[M,0]
$$
with the zero represented at any common stage. The identity of $(E,K)$ is $[E,\operatorname{id}_K]$, using the literal normalization $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$. If $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ and $[N,v]:(F,L)\to(G,R)$, choose a finite $P\supseteq M,N$ and prescribe
$$
 [N,v]\circ[M,u]=[P,v_P\circ u_P].
$$
All scalar-extension functors and associators in these formulas are those specified above.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this construction: the
ledger's verified entries contain no filtered-colimit or Karoubi
construction of coefficient categories, and the blueprint adds the pair
category $\mathcal P_T$ of finite stages, whose morphism sets are filtered
colimits over the finite extensions $E/\Ql$. The nearest entries, each
fetched and quoted, are Categories, Definition 4.21.1 ([Tag
00D3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00D3), directed set) and Lemma
4.21.5 ([Tag 0032](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0032), a filtered
index category may be replaced by a directed set without changing colimits)
with Remark 4.21.6 ([Tag
09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8), a colimit indexed by a
finite filtered category need not be trivial), and Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)), which fixes one
Noetherian coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and forms no colimit over coefficient
fields. Difference: those entries take colimits of diagrams inside a fixed
category and keep the coefficient ring fixed, whereas the blueprint adds
both the filtered poset $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ and the category
$\mathcal P_T$ built from it.

proof.text: Identify the finite-stage completed coefficient map with the existing completed scalar coefficient map by comparing every finite quotient projection. Apply finite scalar-extension preservation at the small field models and use its existing semilinear rational extension. The raw localization universal property fixes the factorization literally, including its object function.

Derive this comparison through the universal derived counit and identify it with the adjoint mate by the normalized derived transpose formula.
